In [[graph theory]], a [[Class (mathematics)|class]] of [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graphs]] is said to have '''few cliques''' if every member of the class has a [[Time complexity|polynomial number]] of [[Maximal clique|maximal cliques.]]<ref name=":0">{{cite proceedings
| last1=Prisner | first1=E.
| date=1995
| contribution=Graphs with Few Cliques
| editor-last1=Alavi | editor-first1=Y.
| editor-last2=Schwenk | editor-first2=A.
| title=Graph theory, combinatorics, and algorithms: proceedings of the Seventh Quadrennial International Conference on the Theory and Applications of Graphs
| pages=945–956
| publisher=Wiley
| location=New York, N. Y
| oclc=30781165}}</ref> Certain generally [[NP-hardness|NP-hard]] computational problems are solvable in polynomial time on such classes of graphs,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Rosgen | first1=Bill
| last2=Stewart | first2=Lorna
| date=2007
| title=Complexity results on graphs with few cliques
| journal=Discrete Mathematics & Theoretical Computer Science
| volume=9 | issue=1 | pages=127-136
| doi=10.46298/dmtcs.387 | doi-access=free}}</ref> making graphs with few cliques of interest in computational [[graph theory]], [[Social network analysis|network analysis]], and other branches of [[applied mathematics]].<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Fox | first1=Jacob | authorlink1=Jacob Fox
| last2=Roughgarden | first2=Tim
| last3=Seshadhri | first3=C.
| last4=Wei | first4=Fan
| last5=Wein | first5=Nicole
| date=2020
| title=Finding Cliques in Social Networks: A New Distribution-Free Model
| journal=SIAM Journal on Computing
| volume=49 | issue=2 | pages=448–464
| doi=10.1137/18M1210459| arxiv=1804.07431}}</ref> Informally, a family of graphs has few cliques if the graphs do not have a large number of large [[Cluster (statistics)|clusters.]]

== Definition ==
A ''clique'' of a graph is a complete [[Subgraph (graph theory)|subgraph]], while a ''maximal clique'' is a clique that is not properly contained in another clique. One can regard a clique as a cluster of vertices, since they are by definition all connected to each other by an edge. The concept of clusters is ubiquitous in [[data analysis]], such as on the analysis of [[social network]]s. For that reason, limiting the number of possible maximal cliques has computational ramifications for [[algorithm]]s on graphs or networks.

Formally, let <math>X</math> be a class of graphs. If for every <math>n</math>-[[Vertex (graph theory)|vertex]] graph <math>G</math> in <math>X</math>, there exists a polynomial <math>f(n)</math> such that <math>G
</math> has <math>O(f(n))</math> maximal cliques, then <math>X</math> is said to be a ''class of graphs with few cliques.''<ref name=":0" />

== Examples ==

* The [[Turán graph]] <math>T(n, \lceil n/3 \rceil)</math> has an [[Exponential growth|exponential number]] of maximal cliques. In particular, this graph has exactly <math>3^{n/3}</math>maximal cliques when <math>n \equiv 0 \mod 3</math>, which is [[Asymptotic analysis|asymptotically greater]] than any polynomial function.<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Graham | first1=R. L. | authorlink1=Ronald Graham
| last2=Knuth | first2=D. E. | authorlink2=Donald Knuth
| last3=Patashnik | first3=O.
| date=1994
| title=Concrete mathematics: a foundation for computer science
| edition=2nd
| location=Reading, Mass
| publisher=Addison-Wesley
| oclc=29357079}}</ref>{{rp|441}} This graph is sometimes called the ''Moon-Moser graph'', after Moon & Moser showed in 1965 that this graph has the largest number of maximal cliques among all graphs on <math>n
</math> vertices.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Moon | first1=J. W.
| last2=Moser | first2=L. | authorlink2=Leo Moser
| date=1965
| title=On cliques in graphs
| journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]
| volume=3 | issue=1 | pages=23–28
| doi=10.1007/BF02760024}}</ref> So the class of Turán graphs does ''not'' have few cliques.
* A [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] <math>T
</math> on <math>n
</math> vertices has as many maximal cliques as edges, since it contains no triangles by definition. Any tree has exactly <math>n-1
</math> edges,<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Pahl | first1=P. J.
| last2=Damrath | first2=R.
| date=2001
| oclc=47208580
| title=Mathematical foundations of computational engineering: a handbook
| location=Berlin ; New York
| publisher=Springer
| doi=10.1007/978-3-642-56893-0}}</ref>{{rp|578}} and therefore that number of maximal cliques. So the class of trees has few cliques.
* A [[chordal graph]] on <math>n
</math> vertices has at most <math>n
</math> maximal cliques,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Gavril | first1=Fǎnicǎ
| date=1974
| title=The intersection graphs of subtrees in trees are exactly the chordal graphs
| journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]]
| series=Series B
| volume=16 | issue=1 | pages=47–56
| doi=10.1016/0095-8956(74)90094-X | doi-access=free}}</ref>{{rp|49}} so chordal graphs have few cliques.
* Any [[planar graph]] on <math>n
</math> vertices has at most <math>8n-16 
</math> maximal cliques,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Wood | first1=David R. | authorlink1=David Wood (mathematician)
| date=2007
| title=On the Maximum Number of Cliques in a Graph
| journal=Graphs and Combinatorics
| volume=23 | issue=3 | pages=337–352
| doi=10.1007/s00373-007-0738-8| arxiv=math/0602191}}</ref> so the class of planar graphs has few cliques.
* Any <math>n
</math>-vertex graph with [[boxicity]] <math>b
</math> has <math>O(n^b)
</math> maximal cliques,<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Spinrad | first1=J. P.
| date=2003
| oclc=51848305
| chapter=Intersection and containment representations
| title=Efficient graph representations
| pages=31–53
| location=Providence, R.I
| publisher=American Mathematical Society
| doi=10.1090/fim/019}}</ref>{{rp|46}} so the class of graphs with bounded boxicity has few cliques.
* Any <math>n
</math>-vertex graph with [[Degeneracy (graph theory)|degeneracy]] <math>d
</math> has at most <math display="inline">(n-d)3^{d/3}
</math> maximal cliques whenever <math>d \equiv 0 \mod 3
</math> and <math>n \geq d+3
</math>,<ref>{{cite conference
| last1=Eppstein | first1=David | authorlink1=David Eppstein
| last2=Löffler | first2=Maarten
| last3=Strash | first3=Darren
| date=2010
| contribution=Listing All Maximal Cliques in Sparse Graphs in Near-Optimal Time
| editor-last1=Cheong | editor-first1=O.
| editor-last2=Chwa | editor-first2=K.-Y.
| editor-last3=Park | editor-first3=K.
| title=Algorithms and Computation
| series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science
| volume=6506
| pages=403–414
| location=Berlin, Heidelberg
| publisher=Springer
| doi=10.1007/978-3-642-17517-6_36}}</ref> so the class of graphs with bounded degeneracy has few cliques. 
* Let <math>G
</math> be an [[intersection graph]] of <math>n
</math> [[convex polytope]]s in <math>d
</math>-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] whose [[Face (geometry)|facets]] are parallel to <math>k
</math> [[hyperplane]]s. Then the number of maximal cliques of <math>G
</math> is <math display="inline">O\left(n^{dk^{d+1}} \right)
</math>,<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Brimkov | first1=Valentin E.
| last2=Junosza-Szaniawski | first2=Konstanty
| last3=Kafer | first3=Sean
| last4=Kratochvíl | first4=Jan | authorlink4=Jan Kratochvíl
| last5=Pergel | first5=Martin
| last6=Rzążewski | first6=Paweł
| last7=Szczepankiewicz | first7=Matthew
| last8=Terhaar | first8=Joshua
| date=2018
| title=Homothetic polygons and beyond: Maximal cliques in intersection graphs
| journal=[[Discrete Applied Mathematics]]
| volume=247 | pages=263–277
| doi=10.1016/j.dam.2018.03.046 | doi-access=free}}</ref>{{rp|274}} which is polynomial in <math>n
</math> for fixed <math>d
</math> and <math>k
</math>. Therefore, the class of intersection graphs of convex polytopes in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space with a bounded number of facets has few cliques.
